newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots promote EU membership.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots promote EU membership.

text.p: A group of pro-European Greek Cypriots announced on Friday a drive to teach people on both sides of the divided island the benefits of belonging to Europe.
"We want to promote the European idea in Cyprus's society among Greek and Turkish Cypriots," said Marios Eliades, chairman of the Zenon group, formed on private initiative.
Greek and Turkish Cypriots live separately in Cyprus, divided by a Turkish invasion in 1974 sparked by a coup in Nicosia backed by the military regime in Greece.

Eliades, a lawyer, told Reuters the group was relying on the United Nations peacekeeping force on the island to help forge links with Turkish Cypriots living in the north. The United Nations is the main go-between for bicommunal activities.

"The European Commission and Brussels have promised all their support to get our message across to the Turkish Cypriot community and especially the younger generation, which hopefully will be able to live with us in the European Union," he said.
The internationally recognised Greek Cypriot government is due to start accession talks with the European Union in 1998.

The Turkish Cypriot side, which declared a breakaway state recognised only by Ankara in 1983, currently opposes EU membership. It says the Cypriot government's application was illegal because it cannot act on behalf of the Turkish Cypriots.
